assessments.reasoning: The dated release entry identifies 3.46.0 as introducing a digit separator in SQL numeric literals and links to the literal documentation. The linked guide supplies the per-gap limit and the effect on the value. I opened the retained original material and verified the complete-body and cited-range digests.

The literal-syntax discussion dates the rule to 3.46.0. Each gap between adjacent digits may contain one underscore, and that character contributes nothing to the literal's value. The release entry independently identifies the same change within the vendor's release history.

challenge.method: Could the release entry alone distinguish one separator per gap from consecutive separators or establish how the separator affects the value? Compare a literal with separators in two distinct digit gaps, one with two separators in the same gap, and quoted text passed to a numeric conversion.
challenge.results: It establishes the introduction and placement. The expressions guide resolves both remaining questions for the same feature and release. The documented rule permits the first spelling. The second exceeds the per-gap allowance. Conversion of quoted text falls outside the literal grammar examined here. These are interpretations of the documentation, not runtime observations.

limitations: This is a numeric literal notation feature. Numeric conversion of arbitrary strings and general SQL portability are outside scope.

The finding concerns numeric literals. The test covers decimal integer examples and the guide supplies the general documented language rule. String-to-number conversion and cross-engine portability are outside scope.
